_doc: #1360 policy of 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-android-perms-guard.py. signatures: a regex in an app's own src/main Kotlin/Java that only works with the catalogue id granted (P1). engines: code that makes ANOTHER fleet app do the work, so that app's grant is the one that matters (P4). not_android: apps whose build.json has an application_id but ship no Android manifest of their own. scan_skip: vendored subtrees whose code no build of this app compiles.

termux-exec.why: the git, rsync and shared-store engines run inside cld.termux; its own All files access decides whether they can touch shared storage

not_android._doc: apps with an application_id whose Android tree is fetched from upstream at build time (no manifest in this repository): the guard cannot read them; their Perms page is the upstream app's own.
not_android.ac_cloud-code: Acode, fetched upstream at build time: its manifest and permission asks are upstream's
not_android.ac_cloud-office: Collabora Office, fetched upstream at build time (materialize): its manifest is upstream's

implied_by._doc: a code need that another declared grant already covers

pending_page._doc: #1360 Gradle apps whose own UI is a vendored fork or a non-Compose host that does not link libs:perms yet: their permissions are DECLARED (build.json::perms, checked P1-P4) but drawn by the fork's own screens. The list may only shrink (pending_page_max).
pending_page.ac_cloud-chat: React Native (Mattermost) host: permissions are asked from JavaScript by the upstream screens

one_place._doc: #1515 P7 of 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-android-perms-guard.py. tokens: calls an app may make only from its Perms page. allow: path substrings of the places that may (the libs:perms lib and each app's declared Perms page). exceptions: declared in data, code that acts on OTHER apps. baseline: sites not moved into a Perms row yet (exact file, or a dir/ prefix for a vendored fork); the list only shrinks (baseline_max) and an entry that stops violating must be removed.

exceptions.why: Background policy (bgpolicy) acts on OTHER fleet apps through the shell broker (cmd appops set, standby bucket); it never changes this app's own grants
